Back in the day everybody I knew completely overlooked the GameCube. Nobody was really proud to own a one. Everybody was rocking PS2 and was into more realistic games which Nintendo wasn't really into making. It's only now that I'm beginning to see what makes the GameCube good. It's basically doing what the N64 wishes it could. There's really no hardware limitations with the GameCube for the kind of games Nintendo was making at the time. The GameCube has the same charme as the N64 but without hardware limitations. It's like an updated N64. That's what makes it a good system , and one that I'm considering purchasing for mainly the Nintendo 1st party releases. F-Zero and the Zelda and Metroid games are pretty much the only games I'm interested in playing, because I'm kinda pissed I didn't get to play these when I was younger. I was always into Nintendo growing up, but after the N64 I kinda lost interest in Nintendo. I think the Dreamcast is what made me say fuck everything, because I traded my PS1 with a bunch of shit for a Dreamcast and pretty much waited for PS2, and then shortly after an Xbox.. The point is, I skipped right over the GameCube and missed some good games for sure.
Anybody else miss out on the GameCube back in the day? Because I'm just starting to see how it's basically what N64 wanted to be.

I'll be honest that most of my Gamecube power on hours were devoted to the Game Boy Player. Plays everything from 1989's Tetris through Samurai Deeper Kyo, with obvious exceptions for Tilt sensing games and the Boktai series. As much as I love my massive GB handheld collection, playing it on a screen is so low on neck and arm fatigue that I'd call it the definitive way to play, despite its few flaws.

But 1st party titles in those days were pretty flawless. It was easy for them to be experimental when they didn't have the pressure of being #1 in the market. Look at new IPs like Animal Crossing and Pikmin, and really experimental twists they made with Zelda (Windwaker's Toon look) and Metroid (Metroid forumula plus FPS). Their games just seemed much more artistically inspired in those days.

When the SNES was on top, there were plenty of really interesting games like Yoshi's Island and Mario Paint, but mostly they let the 3rd parties do the talking with absolutely excellent stuff coming out of Konami, Capcom, and Square. 3rd parties mostly abandoned Gamecube exclusives with very few exceptions for a public that would have easily bought more.
